European Union Free Trade Agreements and Economic Partnership Agreements applicable to Luxembourg as an EU Member State, including CETA (Canada), EU-Japan EPA, and EU-UK TCA

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et contre le financement du terrorisme), as amended from time to time and last consolidated for EU Directives 2015/849, 2018/843 and 2020/0258; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (Loi du 13 janvier 2019 portant création du Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs), as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020; Grand-Ducal Regulations specifying RBE content and filing thresholds; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (Art. 710-1 et seq. governing the SARL); CSSF Circular 20/726 on AML/CFT internal policies and CSSF Circular 22/819 on customer due diligence; FATF Mutual Evaluation Report of Luxembourg (2019) and subsequent follow-up reports.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent public authority of the UBO's/director's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Apostille jurisdictions, Consular Legalization by the Luxembourg consulate or embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the corporate shareholder or ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation of the shareholder or parent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and certified copy of the articles of association/charter of the corporate UBO chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or registered agent of the relevant corporate party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney for the Luxembourg incorporation process and RCS filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds confirmation from the funding institution of the shareholder(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: None - bank-to-bank AML verification; no apostille or legalization required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors and authorised signatories against: the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (including EU Regulation 269/2014 and Ukraine-related designations), the United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list and the OFAC 50% Rule for owned entities, UK OFSI consolidated list, and the Luxembourg national sanctions lists administered by the Ministry of Finance and the Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier). Politically Exposed Person (PEP) identification is mandatory under FATF Recommendation 12 and CSSF Circular 20/726, including family members and close associates, with enhanced due diligence, independent validation of source of funds, and senior management approval for PEP relationships. Negative news, adverse media, regulatory enforcement records and tax good-standing checks are required. Given the Low_Risk_Standard tier for IVD reagent distribution, a written risk justification, standard CDD and quarterly list screening are required, with periodic re-review at least every three years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online portal (www.lbr.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be clearly distinguishable from all existing RCS entries and must not mislead the public. The deed of incorporation may be drafted in French, German or Luxembourgish; the RCS database requires Latin-script indexing, so any non-Latin script must be transliterated into Latin characters with a certified translation where relevant. For a société à responsabilité limitée, the corporate name must be preceded or followed by the words 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL'. Foreign-language names are accepted provided they are not contrary to public order, do not create confusion with local institutions, and are accompanied by a French, German or Luxembourgish translation where the notary considers it necessary.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg (reference to the Grand Duchy or state symbols requiring prior authorization of the Ministry of Justice)
Banque / Bank / banking (requires prior CSSF authorization)
Assurance / Réassurance (requires prior authorization of the Commissariat aux Assurances)
SICAV / Fonds d'investissement / UCITS (requires prior CSSF authorization)
Bourse / Stock Exchange (requires prior CSSF authorization)
Université / École / Institut (requires prior Ministry of Education authorization)
État / Ministère / Administration / Société Nationale (state-adjacent marks requiring ministerial approval)
Croix-Rouge / Red Cross (requires special statutory authorization)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a refusal by the RCS on grounds of confusing similarity, misleading character or missing ministerial authorization, the applicant may: (i) request a reasoned re-examination by the RCS through the LBR portal within one month of the refusal; (ii) if the refusal is maintained, file an appeal with the commercial chamber of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg in accordance with Article 8 of the Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS; (iii) where the refusal relates to a sensitive token, obtain the relevant prior authorization from the competent Luxembourg ministry or regulator (e.g., Ministry of Justice for state-adjacent words, CSSF for banking and fund terms, Commissariat aux Assurances for insurance terms) and re-submit; or (iv) re-file a new name reservation with additional distinctive elements. A reserved name is not renewable by right after the expiry of the 90-day window unless the underlying incorporation file has been duly opened before the notary.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure letterbox or virtual-only office is not permissible as the registered office (siège social) of a Luxembourg SARL. Luxembourg law requires a real and stable seat within Luxembourg with organised local administration. A professional domiciliation company is acceptable and commonly used for ISIC 4649 distribution entities, provided it offers physical accommodation, local receival of mail, maintenance of books, and availability of a contact person for the RCS, the Administration de l'Enregistrement (AED), the tax office, and the CCSS. For this IVD reagent distribution project, the corporate substance requirement must be satisfied by local directors or managers, local board minutes, a local bank account and demonstrable decision-making in Luxembourg; a purely offshore virtual office must be rejected for AML/CFT and substance purposes. The entity should also register as an economic operator within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2017/746 (IVDR) with the relevant Luxembourg health authorities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified annual risk of unannounced on-site inspection at the registered office is approximately 10-20% for a standard low-risk distribution SARL in the absence of red flags. The probability rises to 50% or higher if the entity triggers AED substance questionnaires, intra-Community VAT anomalies, negative RBE inconsistencies, or CSSF/FIU AML file requests. The tax administration and the RCS are legally empowered to verify the registered office without prior notice and to cross-check the physical presence of personnel, records and local management.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), notably Articles 710-1 (minimum share capital), 710-8 (payment of shares; blocked account), 710-10 (notarial deed), 710-11 (registration) and 710-16 (publication); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (Loi du 19 décembre 2002 concernant le registre de commerce et des sociétés); Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Law of 4 July 2014 on Medical Devices, as amended, for the downstream wholesale distribution authorization.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg City, acting through the eJustice / mybusiness.etat.lu single filing portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) executed before a Luxembourg notary, accompanied by the electronic registration application and statutory annexes, including the bank blocked-account certificate, filed with the RCS via the eJustice system.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,000 minimum subscribed capital for a SARL. Each cash-issued share must be paid up to at least 25% of its nominal value at incorporation, and any share premium must be fully paid. The paid-in funds must be held in a blocked account (compte bloqué) at a Luxembourg credit institution, evidenced by a bank certificate annexed to the notarial deed; the funds are released only upon RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the notarial deed of incorporation of the Company, a Luxembourg société à responsabilité limitée, be ratified and approved in full. RESOLVED, that the share capital of EUR 12,000, divided into 120 participating interests of EUR 100 each, be subscribed in full, and that 25% per share be paid into the blocked account at [Bank]. RESOLVED, that the registered office be fixed at [address], Luxembourg. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed gérant with full management powers, authorized to file all corporate, tax and social registrations, open bank accounts, and apply for the wholesale distribution authorization for in vitro diagnostics with the Direction de la Santé. RESOLVED, that the financial year end on 31 December.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name reservation and non-confusion check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), via the mybusiness.etat.lu / eJustice name-reservation portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two or three proposed company names electronically to the RCS. The RCS issues a certificate of non-confusion (certificat de non-confusion) confirming that the chosen name does not collide with an existing legal entity or protected mark. The certificate is valid for three months and must be incorporated into the notarial deed. The corporate object (statut) must expressly include the wholesale distribution of clinical diagnostic ELISA assays and in vitro diagnostic reagents.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application listing proposed names
Short description of the corporate object
Identity documents of the founding partners
Power of attorney if filed through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a negative non-confusion decision, file replacement names immediately through the same portal. A formal refusal may be challenged before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg within 30 days of notification, and trademark oppositions are handled separately by the Benelux Office for Intellectual Property.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked capital deposit account and bank attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution selected by the incorporators; monitored by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The future SARL or its incorporators open a blocked account (compte bloqué) at a Luxembourg bank and deposit at least 25% of the nominal value of each subscribed cash share, plus 100% of any share premium. The bank performs the mandatory AML/KYC checks and issues a certificate of blocked deposit (attestation de blocage) identifying the future company, the notary, the deposit amount and the irrevocability of the blocking. The certificate is delivered to the notary for annexation to the deed of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association
Certificate of non-confusion
Identity cards or passports of natural-person shareholders
UBO and source-of-wealth declarations
Corporate registers and board resolutions for any corporate shareholder
Bank account application and proof of wire transfer of the capital contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the attestation due to AML deficiencies, supplement the source-of-funds documentation or switch to another Luxembourg credit institution. Where a bank route is impracticable, the notary may, where legally available, accept proof of consignment with the Caisse de Consignation; repeat the deposit and re-issue the attestation before the notarial deed is signed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and signing of the notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Notaire) — Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary drafts the statuts (articles of association), verifies the certificate of non-confusion, the bank attestation, the legality of the corporate object, the registered-office lease and the identity of the founding partners, and obtains the gérants' acceptance. The deed is signed before the notary, who then lodges the complete electronic filing package with the RCS through the eJustice system, paying the official filing fee on behalf of the company.
required_dossiers: Certificate of non-confusion
Bank blocked-account attestation
Draft statuts approved by incorporators
Identity documents of all founding partners
UBO declarations
Lease or promise of lease for the registered office
Written acceptance of office by each gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (demande de complément), the notary cures the defect by supplementary filing or by a rectificatory deed within 15 days. Substantive errors require a new notarial act amending the statuts, re-filed electronically with corrected annexes; the original notarial fees remain due but no additional tax is triggered for calendar-year rectifications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration, legal personality and RESA publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS verifies the notarial filing and registers the company in the commercial register. On registration the SARL acquires legal personality, obtains the Luxembourg business registration number (matricule, format RCS Bxxxxxx), and legal effect is given to the statutory documents. The company receives its extract from the RCS and the registration data is automatically transmitted to the competent tax authority and the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) for employer registration; the RCS also arranges publication in the RESA, giving third-party opposability.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation and annexes lodged by the notary
Electronic registration eForm
Certificate of the registered office and domiciliation documents
Statement of authorized signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, request expedition in writing from the RCS and apply for a certified provisional extract. In case of refusal, the company may petition the President of the Tribunal d'arrondissement for an order compelling registration; procedural errors are cured by a rectificatory notarial act immediately re-filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, social, UBO and sectoral operational registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDTV); Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE); Direction de la Santé — Division de la Pharmacie et des Médicaments.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Luxembourg VAT number with the AEDTV immediately upon receipt of the RCS extract; file the municipal business tax (taxe professionnelle communale) and corporate income tax file with the ACD; finalize employer registration with the CCSS for payroll purposes; file the UBO declaration in the RBE within 30 days of incorporation. Before commencement of IVD reagent trading, submit the wholesale distribution authorization application for in vitro diagnostic medical devices to the Direction de la Santé, together with the environmental declaration for the warehousing site and the premises-related fire and occupational clearances.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract and articles of association
RBE beneficial-owner registration form
VAT registration application (formulaire 1)
CCSS employer registration form
Proof of registered office and lease agreement
Gérant identity documents and criminal-record extract
Ministry of Health authorization file for IVD wholesale distribution
Environmental declaration for the classified establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT number is delayed beyond the statutory window, submit a written reminder to the AEDTV with a copy of the RCS extract and escalate to the taxpayer service. If the Direction de la Santé queries the license file, supply the requested technical evidence within 10 working days; if the RBE rejects the UBO filing, correct the identity documents and re-file within the remaining statutory period. Any administrative silence longer than one month entitles the applicant to a formal reminder under Luxembourg administrative procedure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de la Santé — Direction de la Santé, Division de la Pharmacie et des Médicaments, in coordination with the Ministère de l'Économie (import/export formalities) and the Administration de l'environnement (classified-establishment control).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation de distribution en gros de dispositifs médicaux de diagnostic in vitro — wholesale distribution authorization for in vitro diagnostic medical devices issued under the amended Law of 4 July 2014 on Medical Devices and in accordance with EU Regulation (EU) 2017/746 (IVDR), covering storage and distribution of clinical diagnostic ELISA assays and reagents.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Classified-establishment regime under the Law of 15 June 1992 on classified establishments (établissements classés) and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 May 1999 — Class 4 declaration (déclaration) for the warehousing and wholesale distribution of non-bulk diagnostic reagent kits. No full Environmental Impact Assessment is required because wholesale distribution is outside Annex II of the Law of 22 May 2008 on EIA; reclassification to a higher authorization class would occur only if aggregate dangerous-substance inventories exceed the Seveso III Annex I thresholds of Directive 2012/18/EU.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater is generated; only domestic and cleaning effluent is discharged, subject to the commune's sewer discharge regulation (typical limits: pH 6-10, COD < 1,000 mg/L, BOD5 < 500 mg/L, TSS < 600 mg/L, or as fixed by the competent municipal administration). VOC emissions remain de minimis (below 0.5 tonnes/year) and therefore outside the solvent-emissions obligations of the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 20 July 2001. Expired or damaged reagents shall be managed as hazardous or non-hazardous waste under EU Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 (POPs) and Directive 2008/98/EC and consigned exclusively to authorized waste operators.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety attestation issued by the Service National d'Incendie et de Secours (SNIS) following inspection of storage areas, emergency exits, fire extinguishers and alarm systems; annual renewal of the fire-safety certificate with the commune. Occupational workplace clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) under the Labour Code, including verified electrical installation conformity, chemical risk assessment under Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP), manual-handling controls under Directive 90/269/EEC, and first-aid coverage. Structural and storage-load verification by an approved engineering office where heavy racks or mezzanine storage are installed, with the compliance certificate retained in the health and safety file.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax; unified digital access via MyGuichet.lu (guichet.public.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Luxembourg SARL must first execute a notarised deed of incorporation and register with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), which assigns the national identification number (matricule) and RCS number. For VAT, the entity files the VAT registration form (formulaire TVA) with the AEDT through MyGuichet.lu and receives a Luxembourg VAT identification number in the format 'LU' followed by eight digits within approximately two weeks. Non-established foreign companies making taxable supplies in Luxembourg must complete the simplified registration and, if they hold no EU establishment, appoint a tax representative approved by the AEDT. The ACD uses the same matricule for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax assessments.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate US-style check-the-box elections; a resident SARL is mandatorily subject to entity-level corporate income tax. Optional statutory regimes include: (i) fiscal unity (integration fiscale) election under Art. 164bis LIR, available to a parent holding directly or indirectly at least 95% of the SARL's capital, valid for five years and requiring prior approval of the ACD; (ii) VAT grouping election under Art. 58 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, allowing financially, economically, and organisationally linked taxable persons to be treated as a single taxable person; (iii) hybrid mismatch elections and disapplication measures under ATAD (Art. 56a et seq. LIR) to neutralise deductible hybrid payments; (iv) optional IP box treatment under Art. 50quater LIR providing an 80% exemption for qualifying intellectual property income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutee)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general domestic VAT registration threshold applies to a Luxembourg-established SARL; the first taxable transaction in Luxembourg triggers compulsory registration. A EUR 10,000 EU-wide annual distance-sales threshold applies to non-established EU suppliers selling to Luxembourg final consumers; non-EU third-country suppliers must register from the first supply. The wholesale distribution of clinical diagnostic ELISA assays and reagents in Luxembourg is fully taxable with no de minimis exemption for an established distributor.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has not introduced mandatory B2B e-invoicing or real-time continuous transaction controls (CTC); no tax-authority API clearance or digital stamping is required. Invoices in PDF, EDI, Peppol, or other structured formats such as XML are legally acceptable. Mandatory B2G e-invoicing applies to supplies to Luxembourg public authorities: invoices must be transmitted electronically in PEPPOL BIS 3.0 format through the PEPPOL network. VAT returns are filed electronically via the eTVA platform accessible through MyGuichet.lu.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% VAT) applies to the supply of laboratory diagnostic reagents where the SARL demonstrates that: (i) the goods are physically dispatched or transported by the seller or a third party acting on the seller's behalf to a destination outside the European Union, supported by a valid electronic customs export declaration (SAD / EX-A) and proof of exit from EU customs territory; or (ii) the goods are dispatched or transported to another EU Member State to a customer holding a valid EU VAT identification number validated via VIES, with the transport commencing and ending in different Member States; or (iii) the supply qualifies as an exempt intra-community supply under Art. 44 of the Luxembourg VAT Law. Services directly related to the exported goods, such as international transport and freight, may also be zero-rated under equivalent documentary requirements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD / EX-A) with Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / CMR transport document together with the commercial invoice stating Incoterms and CN/HS codes
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT payment evidence demonstrating receipt of the export proceeds
VIES validation printout confirming the customer's EU VAT registration for intra-community supplies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may audit export zero-rating evidence retrospectively for at least five years, extended to ten years where fraud or bad faith is alleged. Failure to substantiate export status, submission of forged customs paperwork, or false inward remittance certificates triggers immediate reassessment of 17% VAT on the full invoice value, default interest at 0.6% per month, administrative fines of up to EUR 100,000, clawback of all zero-rated refunds, exclusion from electronic export procedures, and criminal penalties including imprisonment of up to five years for VAT fraud under the Luxembourg General Tax Law and VAT Law provisions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating in the Eurosystem; banking supervision is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) under Law of 5 April 1993 on the Financial Sector.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies the full liberalization of capital movements under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. The EUR is fully convertible on both current and capital account; no BCL authorization or prior clearance is required for dividends, branch remittances, or loan repayments. Luxembourg imposes no exchange control quota or repatriation deferral. Practical hurdles: only statistical BCL balance-of-payments reporting (via banks) and corporate law's minimum capital and net-asset solvency tests for distributions apply. Profit remittance is unrestricted provided the SARL satisfies the 'treasury test' under the Law of 10 August 1915 (i.e., net assets after distribution must not fall below subscribed capital plus undistributable reserves), backed by the statutory auditor's confirmation if a statutory audit is mandated.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg has no export proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no forced repatriation window. Export receivables for wholesale distribution of diagnostic reagents may be retained in any currency, converted freely, or used directly to settle foreign supplier invoices. The only administrative requirement is VAT invoice / recapitulative declaration alignment and BCL statistical reporting for cross-border settlements executed through resident banks, which is completed automatically by the bank under ECB Regulation 1745/2011 framework.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Current Account (EUR) + Dedicated Collection Account for trade receivables

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility as a secondary non-bank liquidity rail only. Luxembourg recognizes CSSF-authorized Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and EU/EEA EMIs passporting their license under PSD2 (Regulation (EU) 2015/751; Directive (EU) 2015/2366). Vertically integrated global EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Revolut Business) may offer multi-currency IBANs and serve as a collection/disbursement overlay for low-value, recurring trade payments. Legal constraints: EMIs cannot provide credit, deposit-taking is prohibited, client funds are safeguarded not protected by the Luxembourg deposit guarantee scheme (FGDL €100,000 limit applies only to credit institutions). An EMI balance above €10,000 equivalent at any single provider should be avoided; the treasury's principal liquidity buffer must remain with a Tier-1 licensed bank. EMI inbound/outbound wires require identical UBO/KYC documentation as a bank, and commercial invoices must be tagged with the correct HTS/ECICS product classification to avoid frozen-payment exceptions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted in Luxembourg under CSSF Circular 17/655 (relating to AML/CFT) via electronic identification (eIDAS-compliant e-ID), qualified electronic signature, and live video verification. In practice, for a SARL with non-resident shareholders, all Tier-1 banks require at least one senior compliance interview (video conference accepted) of the director/UBO, plus original or apostilled corporate documents. A physical visit to Luxembourg is not statutorily mandatory but materially reduces onboarding time (from 6–10 weeks down to 3–4 weeks). If the SARL is tax-resident in Luxembourg with non-resident economic beneficiaries, banks may demand an in-person meeting at the Luxembourg registered office; this is a policy-based not statutory mandate. Recommendation: schedule a board meeting in Luxembourg on the bank's premises and submit a notarized board resolution appointing the compliance officer and specifying transaction-banding limits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO identification failure: indirect shareholding structure where the controller sits behind a non-EU trust or intermediate holding company; banks require a 25%-plus beneficial owner declaration from the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), with a €250,000 fine for non-compliance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg RBE extract; full capitalization chart; notarized share register; UBO identification declaration (UE form); corporate certificate of incumbency from ultimate parent; trust deed or fiduciary declaration (where applicable); board resolution ratifying UBO identification as of onboarding date.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth / capital contribution insufficiency: initial equity injection exceeding €50,000 while the economic origin of funds is unclear (e.g., aggregated intra-group dividends or family gifted funds without traceability).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of contributing shareholder (past 3 years); certified bank statements showing the remittance chain; dividend distribution minutes with tax voucher evidence (Form 271A / withholding tax certificate if applicable); notarized gift deed or capital contribution agreement; corporate tax clearance (Avis d'imposition) demonstrating lawful accumulation of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/Criminal exposure red flags: counterparties or supplier currents touching sanctioned jurisdictions (e.g., Russian, Iranian, Belarusian ultimate recipients) or inclusion of a PEP (politically exposed person) among shareholders, even as a minority passive investor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions-screening log via a recognized risk intelligence platform (e.g., Dow Jones, Refinitiv World-Check) no more than 10 business days old; PEP declaration from each shareholder confirming no direct management/control; annual compliance attestation (AML declaration) by the SARL's manager; transaction-flow analysis demonstrating no payment routing via sanctioned intermediaries; contractual WEF/OFAC-compliant clauses in supplier purchase agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regulatory license validation for medical devices: bank expects proof that wholesale distribution of in-vitro diagnostic (IVD) reagents is lawful and that the SARL holds proper authorization from Luxembourg authorities (Ministry of Health under Regulation (EU) 2017/746 – IVDR) and any intermediate import licenses (e.g., for non-EU manufacturers).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IVDR Article 16 importer/distributor registration confirmation issued via the Luxembourg Ministry of Health's electronic portal (LU-CEPA / Pharma-LU equivalent); European Authorized Representative contract (if importing from outside EEA); ISO 13485 certificate of the manufacturer; CE-mark declaration per IVDR classification (Class A/B/C/D); Labelling and warehouse conformity statement for the Luxembourg logistics site (Transfusion/Diagnostic Reagents Act 1994 implementing Directive 98/79/EC historical reference).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Primary rail: SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA CT for EUR-denominated intra-EU injections) from the parent shareholder's bank into the SARL's dedicated account held with a Luxembourg Tier-1 bank. Protocol: (1) remitter must quote the payment purpose code corresponding to 'direct investment - equity capital' using the ECB BOP standard (commonly 'C21' unity or bank-specific 'DIRECT/MD' code); (2) narrative field 70(Remittance Information) must state 'A00000001 – CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION – LU_SARL – NOT FOR RETAIL' and reference the notarized deed of contribution and equity register entry; (3) the receiving Luxembourg bank will complete the BCL balance-of-payments statistical report (IQRS/CPE) using the purpose code; (4) verification: upload, via the bank's corporate portal, the board resolution authorizing capital increase, the notarized contribution deed, the updated shareholder register, and proof of the minimum EUR 12,000 paid-up capital requirement under the Law of 10 August 1915 (SARL minimum capital regime). For loans (shareholder advances), use 'loans – intercompany financing' purpose code with a signed shareholder loan agreement and an arm's-length interest rate consistent with Luxembourg transfer-pricing circular (LU TP Circular 56/1 of 27 April 2016).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rail matrix: (1) SWIFT MT103/MT202 COV for majority of non-EEA supplier payments (e.g., manufacturers in Switzerland, USA, Japan, China) – MT103 must carry ISO 20022 (MX equivalent 'pacs.008') data field 'CategoryPurpose' = 'SUPP' and must reference the underlying commercial invoice number; value dating via TARGET2/SWIFT with EUR/USD accounts; (2) Commercial Documentary Letter of Credit (L/C) issuing or advising through the Luxembourg bank via SWIFT MT700/MT707 series for high-value bulk reagent shipments (> €250,000) or when the manufacturer insists on banker's undertaking; all L/Cs must conform to UCP 600 and INCOTERMS 2020 (typically DAP or EXW); (3) SEPA Credit Transfer (SEPA CT) using the MT103/CEPT+ protocol for EU/EEA suppliers, with settlement in central bank money via TARGET2 and no cross-border clearing fee; (4) For intra-group settlements, use netting under an intercompany netting agreement with monthly cycles, quantifying settlement amounts via SWIFT MT101 (pre-notification) and executing final payments via MT103. No Luxembourg-specific clearing tax is imposed; only market-standard banking commissions and rubrics apply (e.g., 0.1%–0.3% LC commission, MT103 fee €10–50).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD and EUR/CHF outright forwards (FX outright) with a Luxembourg-licensed credit institution, tenors up to 12 months, documented under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or FBF (Fédération Bancaire Française) Master Agreement, with CSA collateral if the notional exceeds €5 million
FX swaps (swap achat/vente) for temporary EUR/USD liquidity bridging, permitted without BCL notification; must be recorded under the same ISDA/FBF netting agreement

Currency swaps (cross-currency interest rate swaps) for intercompany loan hedges, accessible to non-financial counterparties under EMIR Article 11 rules – the SARL benefits from the clearing obligation exemption as a non-financial counterparty below the clearing threshold (EUR 3 billion for FX/interest derivatives) but must report derivative trades to a registered TR (e.g., UnaVista) via the clearing member bank

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on CNY, INR, TRY or other restricted emerging-market currencies – legally permissible under Luxembourg law when intermediated by a Luxembourg bank or its branch/affiliate outside the restricted currency's own exchange-control perimeter; because EUR is freely convertible, NDFs are used only where a physical delivery is blocked by the counterparty's central bank (e.g., offshore CNY/USD via the London or Hong Kong market)

OTC FX Options (vanilla calls/puts) on EUR/USD for upside/downside trade-flow protection, subject to the same ISDA/FBF documentation and option premium accounting treatment under IFRS or Lux GAAP as investments in derivatives; hedging transactions must satisfy the EU Hedge Accounting rules under IAS 39/IFRS 9 if the SARL prepares consolidated accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts filing (balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes) with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval required within 6 months of financial year-end; filing due within 1 month after approval and in all cases within 7 months of the balance sheet date; for a 31 December year-end, approval by 30 June and filing no later than 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice by the Public Prosecutor one month after expiry; court-ordered coercive penalty (astreinte) of EUR 50-100 per day until filing; criminal fines of EUR 500-10,000 per director; persistent failure for three consecutive financial years triggers administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS and judicial dissolution

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate (Luxembourg City): 15% state CIT + 7% solidarity unemployment surcharge (equivalent 1.05 percentage points) + 6.75% municipal business tax; municipal rate varies by commune (up to 11.25%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption (100% dividends/capital gains exemption on qualifying holdings of ≥10% or acquisition value ≥ EUR 1.2m); IP regime granting 80% tax exemption (approx 5% effective rate) for net income from qualifying IP under modified nexus; NOL carry-forward unlimited under LIR art. 114 (the template value of 5 is inoperative for Luxembourg); net wealth tax 0.5% applies
